title: Unità 2 · Buon appetito
question: What do I eat, and how do I order?
workingOn: ordering food and talking about meals
canDo: I can talk about others' likes and dislikes.
I can recognize food and mealtime vocabulary.
culture: In Italy colazione is small: a cornetto and a cappuccino, often standing at the bar. Pranzo can be long, and cena is late, often around 8 or 9 p.m. Many restaurants add il coperto, a small charge per person for bread and the table, and tipping is small or optional, not 15-20% like in the US.

grammar.head: prendere and bere: -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ete, -ono
tricks: -ere verbs: o, i, e, iamo, ete, ono. Only lui/lei, voi and loro differ from -are.
bere uses the stem bev-: bevo, bevi, beve, beviamo, bevete, bevono.
Vorrei… = I would like. Learn it as one polite phrase for ordering; the full verb form comes in Italiano 3.
un po' di = some: un po' di pane. Ho mangiato, ho bevuto, ho preso = I ate, I drank, I had.

sentences: For breakfast I drink a coffee.
My sister is having the fish.
A mio padre piace la carne.
A Giulia non piace la verdura.
In Italia la cena è alle otto.
In Italy dinner is at eight.
A pranzo ho mangiato la pasta.

trick: Same for every verb: beviamo, prendiamo, mangiamo.
ho + mangiato. Both words, every time.

forms.why: I had / I ordered = ho preso.
trick: prendere → ho preso. Short and irregular.

forms.why: Vorrei = I would like. The polite way to order.
some = un po' di + the food: un po' di pane.
trick: A little of: un po' di acqua, un po' di pane.

fill.hint: to drink = bere, io form: bev…
lei form of prendere or ordinare: pr… or or…
fill.why: lei → prende (-ere) or ordina (-are). Both work.

fill.hint: The person who serves you: ca…
un po' ___ = a little of: d…

fill.text: Ieri a pranzo ho ___ la pasta.

fill.hint: You ask for it at the end: co…

fill.why: la carne is one thing → piace.

read.title: Al ristorante
passage: Sono al ristorante con la mia famiglia.
I'm at the restaurant with my family.
Io prendo la pasta e mia sorella prende il pesce.
I'm having pasta and my sister is having fish.
Mio padre beve l'acqua e prende un dolce.
My dad drinks water and has a dessert.

listen.en: What do you eat for breakfast?

frames: No, non mi piace la pasta.

listen.en: What do you want to drink?

lines: Shall we eat at the pizzeria?
Sì! Io prendo la pizza. E tu?
Yes! I'll have pizza. And you?
Io prendo la pasta e bevo l'acqua. 🍝
I'll have pasta and drink water.
Perfect! We'll pay the check together.

prompts: Che cosa piace a tua madre?
checks: Dico che cosa piace al mio compagno.

finish: Now I know how to say what I eat and how to order in a restaurant!

idiom.ex: Che profumo! Ho l'acquolina in bocca.
idiom.exEn: What a smell! My mouth is watering.
idiom.note: Said when food smells or looks delicious, before you eat it.

flags: Vorrei is condizionale (Italiano 3). Per the teacher's decision it is taught ONLY as a memorized phrase for ordering (trick 3 and the forms item). Page 3 already introduced vorrei as a chunk, so this is consistent.
Passato prossimo is limited to three chunks: ho mangiato, ho bevuto, ho preso. No chart, no other persons.
Others' likes use A + name / A mio padre piace … . Indirect object pronouns (gli piace, le piace) are not taught; if the teacher wants them, they need their own item.
Reading: Il conto è venti euro is low for a family of three or four with pasta, fish and dessert. Kept as approved; consider a higher number if students know it.
la verdura is singular in vocab (vegetables as a category); le verdure is also common. Both are correct.
Culture claims are Unverified general statements: coperto is common but not charged everywhere; tipping in Italy is optional and small. Dinner time varies by region (later in the south).
Chat uses Paghiamo (pagare, noi, like giochiamo) and insieme, both glossed.
Vocab is exactly the approved 16 words; verbs are in the grammar and sentences.
